description.narrative: In Ethiopia, about 4 million ha of agricultural soil are affected by high soil acidity, which involves significant output losses and increasing pressure on forest areas to compensate for the productivity loss. Lime application, often in combination with other measures of integrated soil fertility management, helps reclaim acidic soils. GGGI has prepared a concept note for a financing mechanism, which allows for scaling up existing activities on soil acidity. The project idea includes two phases: 1) In the project preparation phase, GGGI will deepen the conversation with implementation partners and stakeholders along the value chain including the relevant ministries and public finance institutions to develop the project in detail. This phase needs to define the scope of activities, modalities around the financing mechanism, details around farmers' business model, and the responsibilities of actors. At the end, a full-fledged project proposal needs to be submitted to a donor. 2) In the main project implementation phase, GGGI, jointly with implementation partners, will provide technical assistance to the government.
